name: Downtown Presbyterian Church

dates.altered: The survey states that 'this building's present appearance dates from alterations undertaken in the 1880s'; the Nashville Downtown Partnership records the 1882 interior painting, the removal of the box pews and the 1887 stained glass. The style node's exemplar dates the design to 1848 where the survey's Part I says the cornerstone was laid 28 April 1849; both are recorded and neither is edited.

survey.prepared: Prepared by Anatole Senkevitch, Jr., Architectural Historian, Historic American Buildings Survey, Summer 1970; measured and drawn in the summer of 1971 at the HABS field office, Vanderbilt University.

quotes.text: B. Description of the Exterior: 1. Overall dimensions: Approximately 80'-3" x 137-9". 2. Foundations: Tennessee limestone. 3. Walls: The exterior is a brick veneer laid in stretcher bond. 4. Structural system: Load-bearing masonry walls. 5. Porches: Portico on north front set between two towers has two Egyptian columns supporting a sheet-metal entablature. Entablature has cavetto cornice with triglyph-like gouging and winged orb in center. 6. Chimneys: Seven brick chimneys.
quotes.page: HABS No. TN-17, Part II.B; no page marker legible in the extract span

quotes.text: 7. Openings: a. Doors: Main entry doors have four recessed panels, square panels top and bottom with two rectangular vertical panels between. On either side are smaller double doors in the same pattern. The pylon-shaped surrounds support cavetto cornices ornamented by triglyph-like gouging. b. Windows: The stained-glass triple-hung sash are set in double windows with pylon-shaped surrounds and cavetto cornices.
quotes.page: HABS No. TN-17, Part II.B.7; no page marker legible in the extract span

quotes.text: 8. Roof: a. Shape, covering: Low-pitched gable roof. b. Cornice, eaves: Cavetto cornice on towers, parapet on sides. c. Towers: Brick towers on front corners rise two stories above main structure. The second story of the tower is square and has louvered openings in pylon-shaped surrounds. The third story is octagonal, with louvered openings with no surrounds
quotes.page: HABS No. TN-17, Part II.B.8; no page marker legible in the extract span

quotes.text: Significance: Designed by William Strickland in 1849, the First Presbyterian Church is the largest and best preserved example of an Egyptian Revival church building in America.
quotes.page: HABS No. TN-17, cover sheet; no page marker printed on the cover

quotes.text: PART II. ARCHITECTURAL INFORMATION A. General Statement 1. Architectural character: A fine example of the Egyptian Revival style, this building's present appearance dates from alterations undertaken in the 1880s. 2. Condition of fabric: excellent.

note: Seeded 5 Sep 2026, WP-11.3 Tranche 2, the mid-nineteenth-century city house cluster. The richest survey in the egyptian-revival cluster, and the one that shows what the style does to a plan: 80 ft wide and 138 ft deep, a 1:1.7 rectangle entered on its short end through two columns between two towers. Worth carrying: the survey calls the walls 'a brick veneer laid in stretcher bond' over 'load-bearing masonry walls', which is the node's claim that this is a masonry style in a light-framing age, stated in a wall section. The towers are the anomaly -- Egyptian temples have no steeples, and the surveyor records square second storeys becoming octagonal thirds.
